hypotheses.claim: A provenance-linked compiler chain source_hash -> grammar/parser -> AST_hash -> typed_IR_hash -> semantic_hash -> lowering_version -> artifact_hash -> execution_receipt is a useful necessary audit condition for ClayCode BASE evidence.
support: 0/10,000 false rejects on clean generated source variants
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Independent stage receipts without explicit parent linkage are sufficient for audit/replay.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production compiler audit reconstructs equivalent unambiguous ancestry and detects all tested stale/mixed-stage substitutions without joined identity.

hypotheses.claim: A fully consistent cryptographic provenance/hash chain is sufficient evidence of semantic-preserving lowering.
support_for_refutation: 10,000/10,000 deliberately wrong but self-consistent lowerings passed chain integrity
executed sample expected 12 observed 2 while chain errors=[]
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Hash continuity plus trusted version identity is sufficient because wrong transformations cannot produce a valid chain.
hypotheses.falsifier: A stronger chain construction cryptographically entails the semantic proof/oracle rather than merely recording transformation outputs.

hypotheses.claim: Program semantic identity should be derived after deterministic parse/type canonicalization and remain distinct from exact source/provenance contract identity.
support: Whitespace variant: source_hash differed; AST, typed IR, semantic and artifact hashes matched; contract_hash differed.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Raw source hash can serve as the single identity without harming deduplication, migration, replay or provenance.
hypotheses.falsifier: Repository-wide corpus shows one raw-source identity provides the same equivalence and provenance behavior with no false distinctions.

hypotheses.claim: BASE compiler acceptance should require both provenance-chain integrity and an independent semantic-preservation/translation-validation oracle for each lowered exemplar.
support: Wrong lowerer passed provenance in 10,000/10,000 cases; semantic oracle found 9,996 behavior differences; remaining 4 cases were observationally equivalent because rhs=0.
CompCert and translation-validation literature independently treat source/target behavior equivalence as a separate correctness property.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Application tests alone make per-translation semantic validation redundant.
hypotheses.falsifier: Full app/FRANK suite plus mutation testing demonstrates equal fault detection with lower complexity and no undetected semantic lowering errors.

hypotheses.claim: Compiler/build provenance receipts and Harness runtime TurnTrace receipts should be linked but remain distinct identity layers.
support: Current Harness TurnTraceEnvelope validates runtime causal stages; current probe validates compiler ancestry. Their failure modes differ.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One universal receipt schema can cover compiler provenance and runtime causal traces without ambiguity or bloat.
hypotheses.falsifier: A single schema demonstrates lower complexity and identical detection/replay properties across both corpora.
